paper.title: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5: A Behavior World Model for Robust Whole-Body Control with Environment Interaction
paper.source_version: arXiv v2, submitted 2026-08-23 09:07:15 UTC; versioned PDF SHA-256 312ba5cf6b01a0b25833a12b47912c15fa8ffe809934617d951943fd3b8d859d

decision_relevance.why_admitted: It provides a current, explicit causal interface for screening and projecting infeasible reference commands, plus evaluation regimes for terrain, OOD commands, and recovery. The mechanism is directly relevant to oracle/reference composition, while its controller changes define a hard fixed-trainer boundary.
not_evidence_for: An implemented RL-Sculptor oracle or reference-composition mechanism
Improvement from changing Sam's task reward
A data-matched causal attribution of Table 3 gains to the filter alone
Human-language steering or iterative harness optimization

mechanisms.name: Reference-window latent encoding
mechanisms.description: A 10-frame, 440-D reference window is noise-perturbed and intermittently root-translation-masked, encoded to a continuous 64-D command, and regularized through a training-only finite scalar quantizer, decoder, and cycle-consistency path.

mechanisms.name: Causal behavior world model
mechanisms.description: A six-layer causal Transformer maps proprioception, previous action, and committed latent command to the current action, predicted next proprioceptive state, and a four-component diagonal-Gaussian distribution over the next latent command.

mechanisms.name: Environment-conditioned latent-command filter
mechanisms.description: The previous step's GMM selects a MAP behavior component, tests the raw latent against its Mahalanobis ellipsoid, and radially retracts an OOD command to the ellipsoid boundary while preserving its direction from the component mean.

mechanisms.name: Automatic spatial terrain annotation
mechanisms.description: Kinematic replay detects contact evidence, removes floor and collision-inconsistent points, clusters planar supports, and fits simulator-ready 3D box primitives co-located with each reference motion.

mechanisms.name: Integrated fall-recovery curriculum
mechanisms.description: Some flat-ground episodes begin from synthetic fallen poses, tracking terms are smoothly gated during recovery, and the same tracking policy is trained to stand and resume the reference without switching controllers.

parameters.name: reference_window
parameters.context: Online reference command assembled from joint, root-relative, translation, and gravity blocks.

parameters.name: latent_command
parameters.context: Continuous control latent; quantization is restricted to an auxiliary reconstruction branch.

parameters.name: transformer_architecture
parameters.context: Causal core with rotary embeddings and per-layer KV cache.

parameters.name: next_command_gmm
parameters.context: Diagonal Gaussian mixture over the next latent command.

parameters.name: training_objective_weights
parameters.context: Auxiliary terms added to the PPO loss; next-step terms are masked across episode boundaries.

parameters.name: root_translation_mask
parameters.context: Training-time intermittent access to global root-reference translation; block is zero in deployment and evaluation.

parameters.name: ood_filter
parameters.context: Previous-step MAP-component Mahalanobis test and radial boundary projection.

parameters.name: contact_detection
parameters.context: Per-surface-sample state machine used by automatic terrain annotation.

parameters.name: terrain_sampling_ratio
parameters.context: Controlled terrain-to-flat-ground mixing rate during training.

parameters.name: source_corpus_hours
parameters.context: Retargeted motion corpora and identified spatial-terrain subsets before cleaning/filtering.

parameters.name: tracking_reward_terms
parameters.context: Paper's fixed controller tracking objective. Tracking errors use exp(-||e||^2/sigma^2); this is not Sam's generated task reward.

parameters.name: evaluation_split_sizes
parameters.context: Four held-out evaluation regimes; Fall reuses Standard references with fallen initialization.

parameters.name: reported_primary_results
parameters.context: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5 with deployed R_safe=3 in the sim-to-sim MuJoCo comparison.

parameters.name: terrain_annotation_audit
parameters.context: Human audit of Bones-Seed annotations, 50 random motions per category.

parameters.name: safety_radius_tradeoff
parameters.context: Reported sweep of robustness versus in-distribution tracking fidelity.

failure_modes.name: Checkpoint- and platform-specific radius calibration
failure_modes.description: The authors require R_safe to be recalibrated per checkpoint and platform before the filter is trusted on hardware.

failure_modes.name: Distribution similarity is not physical-risk reasoning
failure_modes.description: The filter identifies commands unlike training experience, so interception of physically infeasible commands is probabilistic rather than guaranteed.

failure_modes.name: Unfiltered first and reset steps
failure_modes.description: The first step and steps after a behavior switch, temporal reset, or PD hand-off pass through unfiltered because no previous-step mixture is retained.

failure_modes.name: Contact-only scene reconstruction
failure_modes.description: Annotation recovers supports actually touched by the motion, not unused surfaces or complete non-supporting scene geometry.

failure_modes.name: Non-data-matched baseline comparison
failure_modes.description: The compared trackers use different corpora and retargeting pipelines; the authors explicitly characterize Table 3 as generalization evidence, not a data-matched ablation.

failure_modes.name: Missing promised ablations and hardware latency
failure_modes.description: The technical report says a broader evaluation with real-robot latency and component ablations will be added later.

failure_modes.name: Hardware-compatible masking degrades root-velocity tracking
failure_modes.description: The paper attributes its 211.1 mm/s Standard root-velocity error versus HoloMotion-1's 121.3 mm/s to intermittent root-translation masking.

failure_modes.name: No public implementation at extraction time
failure_modes.description: The official project page displayed 'Code coming soon' on 2026-08-30, so paper claims cannot yet be checked against a public implementation.

evaluation.name: Standard flat-ground tracking
evaluation.description: AMASS test split, 136 clips, full-length MuJoCo rollouts; reported 76.6 mm MPKPE, 211.1 mm/s root-velocity error, and 96.3% success.

evaluation.name: Terrain-interaction tracking
evaluation.description: Bones-Seed terrain test subset, 150 clips with annotated geometry; reported 93.3 mm MPKPE, 100.7 mm root-position error, and 81.3% success.

evaluation.name: Physically implausible command robustness
evaluation.description: MotionMillion OOD subset, 136 infeasible clips; with R_safe=3 the system reports 158.0 mm MPKPE and 83.1% survival.

evaluation.name: Fallen-initialization recovery
evaluation.description: Standard references initialized from fallen poses; recovery is return to tracking, yielding 99.3% recovery and 1050.6 rad/s^3 mean joint jerk.

evaluation.name: Human audit of terrain annotations
evaluation.description: A strict 200-motion audit reports 92% overall correctness, with category results from 84% to 98%.

evaluation.name: Robustness-fidelity frontier
evaluation.description: Sweeping R_safe measures Standard MPKPE against OOD survival; R_safe=3 is the selected operating point, but the report does not provide a component-isolated ablation table.

evaluation.name: Qualitative hardware interaction and robustness
evaluation.description: Project and paper figures show live-command terrain/object contact, missing-support responses, disturbance recovery, and G1-to-L01 transfer, but no quantitative real-robot latency or success-rate study is reported in this release.

evidence.claim: The pinned public source is arXiv:2608.18234v2; it is a 20-page technical report with 8 figures and 4 tables.
The policy consumes a 10-frame reference through a 64-D latent and jointly emits action, next state, and a four-component next-command GMM from a six-layer causal Transformer.

The causal OOD filter uses the previous-step mixture, MAP component selection, a Mahalanobis-radius test, and radial retraction to the selected ellipsoid boundary; the first/reset step is unfiltered and the deployed radius is tunable.

The annotation pipeline derives 3D support geometry from motion using velocity/deceleration contact detection, penetration filtering, clustering, and oriented-box fitting, then co-locates terrain with its reference.

Training uses PPO over three retargeted corpora, controlled terrain mixing, fallen initializations, recovery gating, force randomization, specified tracking terms, and 4096 or 512 parallel environments depending on geometry.

Four held-out regimes use regime-specific metrics and full-length MuJoCo rollouts; baseline comparisons are not data-matched, and the report defers broader ablations and real-robot latency evaluation.
With R_safe=3, the paper reports 96.3% Standard success, 81.3% Terrain success, 83.1% OOD success, and 99.3% Fall recovery, with the stated errors and jerk.
A human audit of 200 randomly sampled Bones-Seed terrain annotations reports 92% overall correctness under a strict all-support/no-spurious-primitive criterion.
The safety-radius sweep measures a robustness-fidelity frontier and selects R_safe=3 as the reported knee/operating point.

The authors require per-platform/checkpoint filter calibration, describe it as a training-distribution proxy rather than direct risk reasoning, and state that terrain reconstruction is limited to contacted supports.
The official project page did not expose a public code repository at extraction time.
